name: Dreissigacker et al. 2019 CW ResNet
source: Sec. III A text and Fig. 1 (stem block, n residual blocks, end block); residual block 'built according to' He et al. (Ref. 48). No layer table is given.
unknowns: No filter counts, kernel sizes or strides are stated for the stem or the residual blocks.

Residual block internals are drawn as the standard two-convolution basic block of He et al.; the paper only cites that reference, so the convolution count, any batch normalisation and the activations are not confirmed.
The number of residual blocks is 6 for the T=1e5 s networks and 12 for T=1e6 s; drawn once with x6.
Input length is set per case to hold the widest signal twice (not a fixed number); optimiser and learning rate not recovered.
Whether a global pooling or flatten sits before the dense layer is not stated.
notes: Input is the real and imaginary parts of the FFT of single-detector strain, as two channels over frequency bins.
